item.title: Consistency considerations for rare-event importance sampling
item.description: arXiv:2611.10094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of estimating a small probability $p = P(X \in A)$ by importance sampling with auxiliary density $g$, where $X$ is drawn according to some density $f$. We establish a simple necessary and sufficient condition for the consistency of the importance sampling estimator in triangular schemes where the dimension, the densities $f$ and $g$ and the set $A$ may evolve. It allows to refine the results of Chatterjee and Diaconis [Ann. Appl. Probab. 28 (2018), no. 2, 1099-1135] by establishing the exact minimal sample size required for consistency. Moreover, it allows to study the regime $p \to 0$ which, despite being the relevant mathematical regime for rare-event estimations, has received very little attention so far. We perform an in-depth study of the hyperplane case $A = \{x: x^\top u \geq \alpha\}$ with Gaussian densities, showing that in this case, the optimal importance sampling density considerably improves consistency compared to the standard Monte Carlo estimator. However, we conclude the paper with moment considerations which suggest that, whenever the Monte Carlo and optimal importance sampling estimators both converge, convergence may occur faster for the Monte Carlo estimator.
item.dc:creator: Jason Beh, Emilien Flayac, Jerome Morio, Florian Simatos

item.title: Statistical Geometry of Group Actions: Symmetry, Transport, Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2611.10111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study variational inference in the presence of distributional symmetry, focusing on the interaction between two distinct group actions on a sample space: a symmetry action that leaves a reference distribution invariant, and a transport action that generates a parametric variational family by pushforward. By analyzing the algebraic structure of the total transformation group generated by both actions and the induced adjoint representation of the symmetry group on the transport Lie algebra, we establish that the Riemannian gradient of the Kullback--Leibler divergence at the true transport parameter is constrained to lie in the trivial representation of the symmetry group. Consequently, symmetry forces the gradient to vanish along all non-trivial representations. Combining this representation-theoretic constraint with parameter identifiability yields an orthogonal decomposition of the transport Lie algebra into three interpretable subspaces: an identifiability kernel (along which the objective is locally constant), a bias subspace (where the gradient may be nonzero due to model misspecification), and a symmetry-breaking subspace (where the gradient is forced to vanish by symmetry alone). Finally, we characterize the residual bias directions in terms of distributional mismatch between the base model and the standardized target, and derive an explicit Stein-type moment-matching condition that eliminates this bias, extending the location-scale results of (Margossian and Saul, 2025) to general Lie group transformation families.
item.dc:creator: Quentin Berthet, Peter Bartlett, Romuald Elie, Yu-Han Wu

item.title: Divide-and-Conquer is Tail- and Anomaly-Robust: Factor Model Estimation Without Moment Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.10358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study robust estimation of elliptical factor models with abnormal observations and without requiring the existence of any positive moments. In particular, a divide-and-conquer (DC) estimator averages orthogonal projectors onto the full column spaces of small data blocks, and we rigorously establish its probability bound that allows weak and heterogeneous factors. The derived convergence rate is comparable to that of classical principal component estimators, up to the proportion of anomalies. Building on our DC estimator, we propose a split-sample tail- and anomaly-robust (STAR) estimator for the factor number using sample medians of successive projected coordinate ratios, which is shown consistent under mild conditions. Subsequent factor and common component estimation is also discussed, with the rates of convergence spelled out. Remarkably, given an upper bound on the true factor number, our suite of procedures are free from tuning, require no tail-dependent truncation threshold nor solving an optimization problem, admit parallel block computations, and hence has the same computational complexity as the classical principal component methods. Extensive experiments corroborate our theoretical findings, where DC and STAR are comparable and often outperform state-of-the-art competitors. We also illustrate our methods on a portfolio return dataset.
item.dc:creator: Zetai Cen, Han Yan, Haeran Cho

item.title: Removing the floor from Hoeffding and Bernstein inequalities for finite-population U-statistics
item.description: arXiv:2611.10551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $C$ be a uniformly sampled $n$-element subset of a finite population $D$ of size $N$, and let $U_C$ be the complete U-statistic of order $k$ built from a bounded kernel on the $k$-subsets of $D$. We prove a product inequality for the uniform distribution on $\binom{D}{n}$ and deduce from it the comparison $ \log \mathbb{E}\left[e^{\theta(U_C-\mathbb{E}U_C)}\right] \le \frac{n}{k}\log \mathbb{E}\left[e^{\frac{k\theta}{n}(Y-\mathbb{E}Y)}\right]$, where $Y$ is a single kernel value taken at a uniformly sampled $k$-subset of $D$. This yields Hoeffding, Bennett and Bernstein inequalities for $U_C$ with effective sample size $n/k$ in place of the $\lfloor n/k\rfloor$ available so far. The gain is negligible when $n$ is much larger than $k$, but it approaches a factor of two in the exponent when $k$ is close to $n$.
item.dc:creator: Jianhang Ai, Yiming Chen, Ond\v{r}ej Ku\v{z}elka, Yuyi Wang

item.title: Sequential anomaly identification with sampling constraints for composite hypotheses
item.description: arXiv:2611.10921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of sequential anomaly identification with sampling constraints, where multiple independent data sources are observed over time, but only a limited subset can be sampled at each instant. The objective is to identify the anomalous sources while controlling the probabilities of at least one false alarm and at least one missed detection below prescribed levels. An identification policy must jointly determine when to stop sampling, which sources to declare anomalous, and how to allocate observations across sources under the sampling constraints. We seek policies that minimize the expected time to decision to a first-order asymptotic approximation as the error probabilities vanish. The observations from each source follow an unknown density belonging to one of two disjoint sets, corresponding to regular and anomalous behavior. Focusing on a nonparametric framework, which allows greater flexibility in modeling regular and anomalous statistical behavior, we establish general conditions for asymptotic optimality and provide a unified characterization of asymptotically optimal policies for composite hypothesis testing under sampling constraints. Simulation results illustrate the performance of the proposed policies, and the robustness of the nonparametric framework.
item.dc:creator: Aristomenis Tsopelakos, Georgios Fellouris, Olgica Milenkovic

item.title: Financial Connectedness: Heavy Tails andResponse Attribution
item.description: arXiv:2611.11350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A financial market can appear mainly dependent on its own shocks under a variance account and mainly dependent on external shocks under a cumulative-response account. We establish how these opposite diagnoses arise from the same propagation system. For a given cumulative magnitude, squaring gives greater weight to responses concentrated across sources and time. Source priorities can therefore reverse even in stable Gaussian systems with known parameters. Heavy tails raise a separate question: whether the reported shares have a fixed population basis. One innovation with an infinite second moment removes the full network's finite covariance input. We characterize when normalized shares nevertheless stabilize and construct rank-amplitude connectedness, a cumulative-deviation target without finite first or second moments. It can be consistently estimated under local dependence and identification conditions. With fitted dynamics and rank scatter fixed, changing attribution replaces 3.14 names in the daily Top 10 of forty stocks, selecting recipients with greater external persistence relative to their own adjustment. In five futures contracts, mean external share rises from 28.0% to 55.9%, and 70.9% of recipient-dates switch from own to external dominance.
item.dc:creator: Zhu Yuzhao, Shao Jiahui, Liu Dongqi, Li Dan, Hu Xiaoxiao

item.title: Uniform inference for $U$-statistics of exchangeable arrays under degeneracy
item.description: arXiv:2611.11388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many $U$-statistics of row-column exchangeable arrays become degenerate at natural null hypotheses: their convergence rates change and their limiting laws may or may not remain Gaussian. We establish conditions under which inference based on the classical unbiased variance estimator is uniformly valid across these changes, without knowledge of the degeneracy order. It is known that $U$-statistics can be decomposed into orthogonal projections indexed by bipartite graphs. Under uniform fourth-moment assumptions, we establish that the standardized statistic is asymptotically Gaussian and the classical unbiased variance estimator is ratio-consistent, as long as a certain measure of concentration for projections indexed by disconnected graphs tends to zero. Under compactness of the normalized projections, both properties hold if and only if the proportion of variance contributed by disconnected graphs tends to zero. The necessity of this condition follows from a general limit theorem for these $U$-statistics, in which each graph contributes to a Wiener chaos of order equal to its number of connected components. We note that the row-column jackknife variance estimator, although nonnegative, does not generally give a studentized statistic with a standard normal limit in degenerate regimes. We illustrate our theory with an application to estimation and testing based on a distance from product form, exhibiting Gaussian and non-Gaussian limits at various rates depending on the model. We also propose a conservative inference procedure that does not require a Gaussian limit, valid under additional moment and projection conditions.
item.dc:creator: T\^am LeMinh

item.title: Robust Gaussian process regression: posterior contraction
item.description: arXiv:2611.11582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gaussian processes form a popular and flexible class of prior distributions with principled uncertainty quantification, but the Gaussian likelihood on which the corresponding posterior relies makes them highly sensitive to outliers and contaminated observations. We study Gaussian process regression when among the $n$ observations, $m$ of these are possibly contaminated. A generic framework to obtain posterior contraction rates in this setting is considered, from a frequentist perspective as the sample size $n$ and the number of corrupted observations $m$ grow. We adopt a generalized Bayes approach in which the log--likelihood is replaced by a robustified version; we discuss various choices thereof, such as one recently proposed by Altamirano et al. that preserves conjugacy. We investigate the minimax rate of estimation under adversarial contamination in terms of the Sobolev smoothness $\beta$ of the regression function and $m$. The question of building adaptive procedures to both $\beta$ and $m$ is investigated, and we show that a polynomial loss for adaptation must be paid in general. We instantiate our results for Mat\'ern Gaussian process and deep ReLU network priors. Numerical experiments for existing and new robust algorithms are provided, illustrating the practical applicability of our results.
item.dc:creator: Isma\"el Castillo, Paul Egels, Riccardo Lazzarini, Botond Szab\'o

item.title: Sparse Fault Detection in Linear Systems: Equivalence of GLR Tests and $\ell_1$-regularized Least Squares
item.description: arXiv:2611.11625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the detection of an impulsive fault of unknown time and input channel in a linear system with unknown initial state and Gaussian measurement noise. First, we show that the generalized likelihood ratio test, after the initial state is eliminated by projection onto the parity space, is the zero-solution test of a weighted lasso with an unpenalized nuisance block; the regularization parameter is the test threshold, and for unknown noise variance the same holds for the square-root lasso. Second, we show that the null distribution depends on the system only through a Gram matrix, so that the threshold is computed exactly and offline, and we compare it with closed-form bounds. Third, we characterize the fraction of a fault that survives the projection: we give it in closed form through observability Gramians, we show that it converges to a geometrically decaying profile for strictly stable systems, and that, for systems with unit-modulus modes, it grows linearly with the fault time as a fraction of the record length. Numerical studies, including a two-input, two-output example, illustrate the results.
item.dc:creator: Rajasekhar Anguluri

item.title: On the robustness of locally D-optimal designs under parameter uncertainty in single-factor generalized linear models
item.description: arXiv:2611.11785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local and Bayesian approaches to optimal experimental design specify information about the regression parameters through a nominal value and a prior distribution, respectively. A practical question is whether accounting for parameter uncertainty justifies replacing a locally optimal design. We investigate when locally D-optimal designs remain Bayesian D-optimal in single-factor Poisson, gamma and logistic regression on the unit interval. Analytical arguments and numerical comparisons under normal and uniform slope priors examine how prior form and dispersion affect the optimal support and the Bayesian D-efficiency of retaining a local design.
item.dc:creator: Osama Idais

item.title: An iterated-logarithm price of anytime validity for log-optimal e-processes
item.description: arXiv:2611.11874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Log-optimal e-variables at fixed horizons, also called num\'eraires, have been conjectured to ``almost'' form an e-process for exponential-family null hypotheses. A related open question is whether an e-process can attain the optimal e-power at every horizon up to a bounded loss. Given a final horizon, we study the minimax regret of e-processes relative to the num\'eraires at all times up to it. For the Gaussian location null and the composite alternative of Gaussian distributions with a smaller variance and an unknown location, we show that the minimax regret in the worst case over the location grows like the iterated logarithm of the final horizon. A single e-process attains this rate at every horizon. This growth answers the question negatively. It also refutes the conjecture if ``almost'' means a regret bounded uniformly over horizons. For this Gaussian location problem, we thus exhibit the frontier precisely: the minimax regret is bounded if and only if the alternatives have at least the variance of the null.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Corenflos

item.title: Coverage and shape of conformal highest-density sets: A minimax theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.11909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study conditional coverage and geometric efficiency of conformal highest-density sets. The excess volume of such a set over the conditional highest-density set, the smallest set with the required conditional coverage, splits into a coverage error and an excess mass. We show that, among procedures whose volume is accurate up to a constant, the coverage error has the minimax rate of nonparametric regression on the covariate, and that the excess mass has the squared minimax rate of conditional density estimation. The usual split conformal construction calibrates these sets with a single threshold, which corrects the bias of the density estimate only on average over the covariate. We prove that its coverage error can then be of the order of the slower density rate. We therefore propose two-stage calibration, which estimates the coverage of the super-level sets of a density estimate by a regression on the covariate and uses this estimated coverage as the conformity score. Since these sets are fixed at each covariate value, their coverage is as smooth as the conditional density, and, under mild regularity conditions, the coverage error attains the regression rate even when the density estimate is inconsistent. The shape of the set still depends on the accuracy of the density estimate: sup-norm accuracy controls it at the minimax excess-mass rate, whereas accuracy in an integrated norm, even of minimax order, does not. With a local polynomial density estimate, two-stage calibration attains both minimax rates up to logarithmic factors. Simulations and an application to bike-sharing demand illustrate the results.
item.dc:creator: Ilsang Ohn

item.title: On the Instance-Specific Sharp Rates for Constrained Least Squares Estimators in the Sequence Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.11959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a general methodology based on the Feature Space Decomposition framework for establishing explicit, instance-specific sharp rates for the expected estimation error of convex-constrained least squares estimators in the sequence model, without requiring estimates of localized Gaussian mean widths. We apply this methodology to $\ell_q$ ellipsoids, $\ell_1$ balls, and $kB_1^N\cap B_\infty^N$, obtaining matching upper and lower bounds in the nondegenerate regime. Our methodology also extends beyond Gaussian noise to symmetric noise distributions satisfying a Poincar\'e inequality. We also provide an elementary proof of the instance-specific sharp rate for isotonic regression for any well-specified signal and any noise level. Combining this result with Han's asymptotic reduction, we further obtain explicit instance-specific sharp convergence rates in probability for isotonic regression in Gaussian linear regression under general signal-dependent asymptotics conditions.
item.dc:creator: Zong Shang

item.title: Minimum cumulative power divergence estimation with applications to copulas
item.description: arXiv:2611.12203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parametric inference based on distribution functions is useful when a model is naturally specified through its cumulative distribution function or when a tractable density is unavailable. We study minimum cumulative power divergence estimation, obtained by comparing a parametric distribution function with its empirical counterpart. For a fixed positive tuning parameter and a fixed finite integration measure, we establish the existence of a consistent sequence of local solutions to the estimating equations and derive its asymptotic normality. The resulting covariance has a sandwich form whose components involve derivatives of the distribution function and the covariance kernel of the multivariate empirical process. We specialize the construction to copulas using Lebesgue measure on the unit cube, and distinguish estimation with known margins from estimation based on ranks. In the latter case, the covariance incorporates the effect of estimating the marginal distributions. The relationship with the copula divergences of Eguchi and Kato is made explicit: the power loss is closely related, whereas the integration measure determines a different estimation criterion. A simulation design for Gumbel, Clayton, and Frank copulas examines the estimation of Kendall's tau under correct specification, family misspecification, and contamination by independence. The simulations show competitive clean-data accuracy but no general robustness advantage over the empirical-copula-weighted alternatives under independence contamination.
item.dc:creator: Ostap Okhrin, Konstantinos Zografos

item.title: Linear Functional Estimation under Multiplicative Measurement Error with Unknown Error Distribution
item.description: arXiv:2611.12516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we consider i.i.d. observations from a multiplicative deconvolution model, i.e. generated by $Y= X\varepsilon$, where $X$ and $\varepsilon$ are independent strictly positive random variables. The goal is to statistically infer the unknown signal $X$. Starting from the scenario where the probability density $f_\varepsilon$ of the error is known, we revisit local estimation strategies for several quantities of interest including the probability density function f and the survival function $S^X$ of the signal $X$. We use these results to propose a thresholded plug-in estimation technique for linear functionals in situations where the distribution of the error $\varepsilon$ is unknown, while having some additional data at our disposal. This estimation procedure combines the reconstruction of the unknown Mellin transform of $f$ as well as its regularized inversion by a spectral cut-off. We establish oracle-type upper bounds and discuss rates of convergence in explicit scenarios including estimating $f$ and $S^X$ pointwise. In addition, we develop a fully data-driven choice of the cut-off parameter via model selection, which is able to obtain the oracle risk up to a constant without any previous knowledge of the error distribution. The results are illustrated in a simulation experiment, where we compare different classes of distributions in settings with known and unknown $f_\varepsilon$.
item.dc:creator: Jan Johannes, Maximilian Siebel

item.title: A Strict Upper Bound for Three-Point Weighted Selection in Planar Vector-Valued Regression
item.description: arXiv:2611.12550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove $F_{\mathrm{weighted}}(2,2,3)<11/6$ for minimum-Frobenius-norm least-squares regression with two input and two output coordinates, improving the upper bound $15/8$. More precisely, a universal $\varepsilon_0>0$ satisfies $\mathcal T_3\le(5/6-\varepsilon_0)E$ for every finite residual frame. The proof combines an exact scalar certificate, rigidity of equality in planar selection, and a compactness argument that controls disappearing weights. Together with the known lower bound, this gives $13/8\le F_{\mathrm{weighted}}(2,2,3)<11/6$. No numerical value of $\varepsilon_0$ is claimed.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Volkov

item.title: Riemannian Ordinary Least Squares
item.description: arXiv:2611.10459v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many scientific responses take values in Riemannian manifolds, with predictors that are scalar- and/or manifold-valued. A regression analysis in such settings must provide accurate prediction with hypothesis testing for individual coefficients. Yet no current manifold-regression framework accommodates both predictor types and enables per-coefficient hypothesis tests. We propose Riemannian Ordinary Least Squares (ROLS) as a tangent space conditional-mean model, which is the ordinary least squares (OLS) analogue for Riemannian manifolds. ROLS is well-defined under an explicit injectivity condition that keeps the logarithm maps single-valued, with cut-locus conditions for branch-sensitive cases outside it. Within the local geometric setting it admits a closed-form estimator, an $O(n^{-1})$ excess prediction-error bound with explicit curvature bias, and asymptotic $t$- and Wald tests for individual coefficients. With synthetic simulations and three real-data case studies, ROLS is shown to be competitive with the state-of-the-art baselines. In addition, the per-coefficient tests agree with effects reported in literature. We envision ROLS to be a standard tool for manifold-valued regression with coefficient-level inference to support scientific discovery, which can be interpreted in the same way as Euclidean OLS. The source code is available at https://github.com/XiaoyuChenPub/ROLS.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Xiaoyu Chen, Yujing (Zipan) Huang, Yingyan Zeng. Riemannian Ordinary Least Squares. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), 2026
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyu Chen, Yujing Huang, Yingyan Zeng

item.title: Group-Conditional Conformal Risk Control: Exact Guarantees, Limits, and Overlapping Extensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.10472v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study group-conditional conformal risk control (CRC) for disjoint and overlapping groups under bounded monotone losses. For disjoint groups, we establish exact finite-sample conditional risk control, two-sided bounds on the group-restricted risk, and fundamental limitations arising from local support and calibration-rank granularity. For overlapping groups, we study two exactly valid approaches: group-restricted calibration followed by union deployment, and direct calibration of the deployed prediction-set family. We characterize the union's limiting reconciliation gap, identify conditions for its disappearance, and establish sharp lower bounds for structured losses in specified product-form models. We also demonstrate a strict size advantage for direct calibration in an ordinal model. Experiments show that direct calibration can reduce prediction-set size, but its efficiency depends on group structure, loss type, and shape fitting. Results on historical diabetic-retinopathy scores further illustrate these tradeoffs. Overall, local support, reconciliation slack, and threshold heterogeneity determine efficiency, with neither approach uniformly dominating.
item.dc:creator: Tareq Aldirawi, Wenge Guo

item.title: Periodic Readout Induces a First-Order Generalization Transition in a Quantum Perceptron
item.description: arXiv:2611.10887v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Variational quantum classifiers can generate highly structured decision boundaries through the Fourier dependence of observable expectation values on circuit parameters. We show that expressivity can come at a sharp statistical cost, by considering a quantum perceptron whose readout is the simplest periodic classifier, namely a square-wave function of the weighted inputs, and determine its typical generalization in the thermodynamic limit using a teacher-student replica-symmetric theory. Above a critical oscillation frequency, increasing the training load induces a first-order transition from weakly to strongly teacher-aligned phases, resulting in a discontinuous improvement in generalization. At fixed load, however, increasing the frequency eventually drives the equilibrium generalization error to chance level, despite perfect classification of all the training examples. Thus, the same periodic structure that enhances random-label storage can delay the onset of learning. Our results expose a quantitative tradeoff between memorization and generalization generated purely by periodic readout, and provide a benchmark for understanding Fourier-rich variational quantum classifiers.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Benatti, Masoud Gharahi, Giovanni Gramegna, Stefano Mancini, Vincenzo Parisi

item.title: A Unified Framework for Robust Blinded Sample Size Re-estimation Based on Nuisance Parameters
item.description: arXiv:2611.10957v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Blinded sample size re-estimation aims to mitigate uncertainty in nuisance parameters at the design stage while preserving the integrity of the trial. It allows the required sample size to be updated without revealing treatment assignments and thereby reduces the risk of an inappropriate sample size. Although numerous procedures have been proposed for different outcome types, a unified framework is still lacking. We therefore develop a general framework for blinded sample size re-estimation based on nuisance parameters. Within this general framework, we develop robust methods to reduce the influence of extreme observations. The proposed framework combines asymptotically linear estimators for the parameter of interest with robust Z-estimators for nuisance parameters, thereby unifying a broad class of existing procedures through different choices of estimating functions. We also propose a general principle for constructing nuisance parameters that can be estimated from blinded data. The proposed framework is supported by asymptotic theory showing that the type I error rate converges to the nominal level under regularity conditions. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed method maintains reliable type I error control across a range of settings, including contaminated data and small pilot sample sizes. Compared with existing blinded and unblinded methods, the proposed framework is more flexible and less sensitive to outliers. A clinical trial application illustrates its practical utility.
item.dc:creator: Long-Hao Xu, Lei Li, Tim Friede

item.title: Heavy tails in Gaussian-process surrogates: process-level profiling degeneracy versus observation-level identifiability
item.description: arXiv:2611.11188v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we study heavy-tailed alternatives to Gaussian-process surrogates, namely Student-$t$ processes, $\alpha$-stable processes and Gaussian processes with heavy-tailed noise. These are Gaussian scale mixtures, and the position of the mixing variable decides whether the tails can be learned from a single realization. For process-level mixtures with a free amplitude, the profile likelihood of the mixing law is data-free and is maximized by the Gaussian law, the plug-in predictive is a data-free transformation of the Gaussian-process predictive, and no estimator can be consistent for the mixing law over the model along one path. For observation-level mixtures with symmetric $\alpha$-stable noise, the tail index is identifiable. Further, for one-dimensional inputs under fixed-domain asymptotics with $\alpha_0<2$ and compact hyperparameter sets, a cross-fitted plug-in estimator and the Laplace marginal-likelihood estimate computed at the global posterior mode attain the efficiency bound of the model with a known regression function, also for Mat\'ern-$5/2$ sample paths. We also characterize small-sample failures of the Laplace approximation as folds of a posterior-mode branch and give a diagnostic. Finally, in a repeated Bayesian optimization study, observation-level tails reduced regret under gross outliers, as did Student-$t$ noise, and no degradation was detected under Gaussian noise.
item.dc:creator: Neelesh S. Upadhye, Rohit Kumar Mani

item.title: Fingerprints of feedback cycles in stationary diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2611.11288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When does the stationary density of a $d$-dimensional diffusion process driven by standard Brownian motion uniquely determine its drift? In general, it does not: the $d$ drift components enter the stationary Fokker-Planck equation only through a single scalar divergence. We consider drifts whose component functions only depend on a subset of their input variables, and encode this dependence with a directed graph. We exclude 2-cycles, which admit rotations that leave the stationary density invariant, but otherwise allow arbitrary graphs, including those with feedback cycles. We show that if the stationary density is sufficiently $s$-concave, e.g., strictly log-concave, then the drift is uniquely determined among graph-structured drifts in a weighted Sobolev space. For drifts with linear self-regulation, a single locally strictly convex level set of the stationary density is sufficient to identify the drift in the region it encloses. Both results follow from Raychaudhuri equations. Excluding 2-cycles allows treating nontrivial rotational and symmetric terms simultaneously, extending the scope of the corresponding Bochner- and Reilly-type arguments. We illustrate the results by recovering the Hill-type regulation of a stochastic genetic repressilator from samples of its stationary distribution.
item.dc:creator: Richard Schwank, Mathias Drton

item.title: Model-assisted semi-supervised estimation of the Mann-Whitney probability under right censoring
item.description: arXiv:2611.11456v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study semi-supervised estimation of the full-lifetime Mann-Whitney probability under right censoring using finite covariate-only samples from two populations. A model-assisted estimator is constructed by adjusting censored pair comparisons with differences between labeled and auxiliary feature means. Resource weights minimize first-order variance within the working projection class. Under joint independent censoring and regularity conditions, we establish consistency and asymptotic normality through a four-pool influence representation that accounts for censoring distributions estimated from the same labeled records. Consistent variance estimation from all four sample pools yields Wald confidence intervals. The efficiency analysis relates variance reduction to projected comparison signals and auxiliary sample sizes and characterizes the gap to the semiparametric bound. A fixed-horizon extension accommodates half-weighted ties and the terminal mass induced by capping follow-up. Simulations show increasing precision gains with auxiliary sample size under moderate or strong projected signals, with finite-sample losses in some settings with zero or weak projected signals. A five-year Rotterdam breast-cancer comparison illustrates precision gains and variability across label allocations when auxiliary samples are formed by controlled outcome withholding.
item.dc:creator: Hengyao Xu, Tao Tan

item.title: Nonasymptotic causal structure learning in generalized linear DAGs with continuous optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.11667v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the problem of learning directed acyclic graphs from observational data in nonlinear models and provide finite-sample, nonasymptotic statistical guarantees in these models. Although widely studied, statistical guarantees for gradient-based methods in nonlinear models are missing from the literature. Under a generalized linear model for each node, we analyze a global nonsmooth objective combining an exact acyclicity constraint with a quasi-minimax concave penalty, which can be optimized via standard gradient-based solvers. We establish finite-sample guarantees under this model, including the most widely used logistic and Poisson models. Experiments corroborate structure recovery accuracy and computational performance, including both standardized data and negative controls as baselines.
item.dc:creator: Chang Deng, Inbeom Lee, Bryon Aragam

item.title: Distribution-Free Symmetry Detection in Multi-Reference Alignment at Low SNR
item.description: arXiv:2611.11872v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Symmetry can reveal the structure of a signal, but detecting it becomes difficult when observations are noisy and randomly transformed. We study how to infer symmetry directly from multi-reference alignment data with additive isotropic Gaussian noise of known variance, without aligning the observations or knowing how the transformations were sampled. For cyclic symmetry, we identify a simple statistical signature that yields tests with exact finite-sample error guarantees. We demonstrate their performance even at very low signal-to-noise ratios. Dihedral symmetry presents a deeper challenge: we show that, for some signals, invariant moments below a sharp order threshold cannot distinguish reflectional from purely rotational symmetry. For generic signals, however, this distinction emerges much earlier. We use these insights to develop tests for dihedral symmetry with asymptotic error control under explicit nondegeneracy conditions. Together, the results clarify what we can learn about symmetry from noisy, unaligned data and suggest a path toward symmetry inference in cryo-EM.
item.dc:creator: Nir Sharon, Sheng Xu

item.title: CRAFT-GBM: Selecting Best Features for Gradient-Boosted Machine Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.11914v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Feature subsampling is used to accelerate gradient-boosted trees, yet standard approaches fix the feature count in advance and largely ignore the split-gain evidence accumulated during training. We introduce CRAFT-GBM (Confidence-Ranked Adaptive Feature Tracking), a native LightGBM extension that uses this evidence to adapt which---and, by default, how many---features are searched each boosting round. CRAFT-GBM transforms root-split gains into bounded observations and constructs joint time-uniform bounds valid under adaptive, non-stationary training histories. In its default endogenous mode, after initialization, CRAFT-GBM retains exactly the features that cannot yet be ruled out as best, letting the selected feature-set size $K_t$ emerge from training history rather than a pre-specified fraction. With probability at least $1-\delta$, every feature with the largest expected gain is retained jointly across all rounds after initialization. When a feature fraction $f$ is specified instead, CRAFT-GBM ranks features by their interval point estimates and provides an approximate top-$K$ guarantee for feature budget $K_f$. We implement CRAFT-GBM within LightGBM while preserving its native feature-bundling representation, and evaluate it across 14 public and synthetic dataset families and four noise-augmented settings. In the fully endogenous setting, CRAFT-GBM reduces per-fit training time by 39.74\% with 1.04\% lower test loss in the geometric mean across all 18 RQ1 experiments. Under pre-specified feature fraction $f$, Exogenous CRAFT-GBM also yields aggregate training-time reductions up to 13.52 percentage points larger than random feature subsampling, with no increase in aggregate test loss relative to full-feature LightGBM. Accumulated training evidence can thus support adaptive feature search with statistical guarantees while retaining the practical advantages of native gradient boosting.
item.dc:creator: Basil Kuok, Yi Zhou, Yao Xuan, Shuping Li, Ke-Wei Huang

item.title: Conformal Prediction for Multi-Step Forecasting: Conditional Coverage and Sharp Score Calibration Rates
item.description: arXiv:2611.12004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Uncertainty quantification in prediction is a central problem in statistics and machine learning. Conformal prediction provides a flexible approach to constructing prediction sets with valid marginal coverage under exchangeability. In this paper, we investigate conformal prediction for both one-step and multi-step forecasting from a single stationary time series, addressing temporal dependence and the additional challenges of joint prediction across multiple horizons. We propose a kernel-based framework, called Time series Residual Analysis for Calibration with Kernels (TRACK), for estimating conditional quantiles of residual scores and constructing prediction sets from rolling-window forecasters. The framework accommodates heterogeneous uncertainty across horizons and accounts for dependence induced by rolling estimation, while allowing predictor memory and forecast horizons to grow with the sample size. Our finite-sample bounds quantify how temporal dependence and overlapping score windows affect calibration and coverage. We further derive bounds for conditional quantile estimation and pointwise conditional coverage discrepancy. The guarantees extend to more general predictors that admit an accurate rolling-window approximation. We also derive matching minimax bounds over classes of known score maps, clarifying how overlapping score windows affect calibration accuracy. Experimental results from simulations and applications to wind energy generation and bike sharing demand show that our methods improve regional conditional coverage while maintaining competitive interval widths.
item.dc:creator: Siyuan He, Yuhong Yang

item.title: Total variation error bounds for Schr\"odinger-F\"ollmer samplers
item.description: arXiv:2611.12447v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sampling from high-dimensional, multimodal target distributions plays a fundamental role in scientific computing, statistics and machine learning. Recently, the Schr\"odinger-F\"ollmer sampler (SFS) has been proposed by Huang et al. (IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory, 2025) as an efficient sampling algorithm that transports the degenerate distribution at $t=0$ to the target distribution at $t=1$, without relying on long-time ergodicity. In this paper, we establish non-asymptotic error bounds for SFS in the total variation distance by deriving regularization estimates for the associated Kolmogorov equation via the Bismut-Elworthy-Li formula. When the drift can be computed exactly, a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|)$ was obtained under certain smoothness conditions on the drift with a uniform time step-size $h>0$. When the drift is approximated by Monte Carlo methods, we obtain a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|+ 1/M)$, where $M$ is the number of samples used in the Monte Carlo approximation. This yields a sharper dependence on $M$ than the existing bound $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{M})$ in the $L^2$-Wasserstein distance in the aforementioned paper, by turning the total variation error to the weak error analysis in the setting of non-smooth test functions. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the convergence rate with respect to the time step-size $h$ and the Monte Carlo sample size $M$ and the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojie Wang, Xiaoyan Zhang

item.title: Near-Purity Screening and Dominant-Atom Estimation in Softmax Mixtures and Their Ensembles
item.description: arXiv:2611.12647v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study near-purity screening and dominant-atom estimation in softmax mixtures, whose components share a common set of category features. A mixture is called $\varepsilon$-pure if one of its mixing weights is at least $1-\varepsilon$. We introduce the Trace of Latent Covariance Criterion ($\mathrm{TLC}^{2}$), a direct estimator of the trace of the covariance matrix of the latent mixing measure, constructed without estimating its atoms or weights, or knowing the number of components. Unlike existing moment-based approaches, our estimator is constructed for the softmax family and does not require knowledge or estimation of the feature distribution. We establish finite-sample guarantees for $\mathrm{TLC}^{2}$, showing that it achieves a parametric convergence rate up to an additive approximation error of order $p^{-1/2}$, without requiring minimum separation between mixture atoms. We also study estimation of the dominant atom in near-pure mixtures by fitting a single softmax component. We prove that the resulting maximum likelihood estimator has an error bound consisting of the usual parametric term and a bias term governed by the weighted distances between the dominant and remaining atoms, revealing adaptation to the geometry of the mixture. Finally, we extend near-purity screening and dominant-atom estimation to ensembles of softmax mixtures with shared atoms and mixture-specific weights. We apply $\mathrm{TLC}^{2}$ separately to each ensemble member to screen for near-purity without knowing the number of components. Under additional assumptions, clustering the resulting dominant-atom estimators yields finite-sample guarantees for estimating the shared atoms. An application to the Million Song Dataset illustrates how the estimated softmax directions reveal interpretable structure in the data.
item.dc:creator: Xin Bing, Florentina Bunea, Marten Wegkamp, Weicheng Wu

item.title: Distributional Limits of Empirical Codegree Processes in Sampled Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.12853v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study fluctuations of empirical distributions of normalized codegrees under independent vertex sampling from deterministic or random weighted parent networks. We establish a quantitative multivariate normal approximation for sampled biclique counts. Under additional graph-limit and sparsity assumptions, we establish convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions of the empirical codegree process indexed by smooth test functions. We further establish functional convergence on H\"older balls, with a smoothness threshold depending on network sparsity and vertex sampling probabilities. We verify our assumptions for classes of graphon-generated random graphs and give counterexamples showing that the smoothness conditions cannot in general be weakened.
item.dc:creator: Victor Daniel, Sumit Mukherjee

item.title: On the (In)Compatibility between Group Fairness and Individual Fairness
item.description: arXiv:2401.07174v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the compatibility between utility-optimized statistical parity and individual fairness. While individual fairness seeks to treat similar individuals similarly, optimal statistical parity aims to provide similar treatment to individuals who share relative similarity within their respective sensitive groups. Although both fairness perspectives are desirable, they often conflict in practical applications. Our goal in this work is to analyze the existence of this conflict and its potential solution. In particular, we establish sufficient (sharp) conditions for the compatibility between the optimal (post-processing) statistical parity $L^2$ learning and the ($K$-Lipschitz or $(\epsilon,\delta)$) individual fairness requirements. When a conflict arises, we first relax the optimal statistical parity solution to the Pareto frontier, representing the optimal trade-off between $L^2$ error and statistical disparity, and then examine its compatibility with individual fairness. Our analysis identifies regions along the Pareto frontier that satisfy individual fairness constraints. Additionally, we provide individual fairness guarantees for the composition of a trained model with the optimal post-processing step, enabling practitioners to assess the compatibility of post-processed models. This provides practitioners with a principled approach to achieving Pareto-optimal statistical parity while maintaining individual fairness constraints.
item.dc:creator: Shizhou Xu, Thomas Strohmer

item.title: M-estimation for Gaussian processes with time-inhomogeneous drifts from high-frequency data
item.description: arXiv:2508.01164v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study drift and covariance estimation for a stationary Gaussian process with an integrated deterministic drift, observed at high frequency over an expanding time horizon. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality of an increment least-squares estimator under conditions on drift accumulation and the full covariance of the weighted increments. For directly Riemann integrable drifts, this estimator need not be consistent, as an explicit example shows. Covariance parameters can nevertheless be estimated consistently when the drift decays sufficiently fast. For smooth short-range kernels, we prove a joint central limit theorem for the centered sample variance and the normalized increment second moment, with rate $\sqrt{T_n}$. These statistics require no drift estimate and identify both parameters of the Gaussian kernel. The results clarify how drift accumulation and increment dependence affect the two estimation problems.
item.dc:creator: Yasutaka Shimizu

item.title: Statistical Inference for Rates of Change in Spatial Processes over Riemannian Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2601.02305v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Statistical inference for spatial processes from partially realized or scattered data has seen voluminous developments in diverse areas ranging from environmental sciences to business and economics. Inference on the associated rates of change has seen some recent developments. The literature has been restricted to Euclidean domains, where inference is sought on directional derivatives, rates along a chosen direction of interest, at arbitrary locations. Inference for higher order rates, particularly directional curvature has also proved useful in these settings. Modern spatial data often arise from non-Euclidean domains. This manuscript particularly considers spatial processes defined over compact Riemannian manifolds. We develop a comprehensive inferential framework for spatial rates of change for such processes over vector fields. In doing so, we formalize smoothness of process realizations and construct differential processes -- the derivative and curvature processes. We derive conditions for kernels that ensure the existence of these processes and establish validity of the joint multivariate process consisting of the ``parent'' Gaussian process (GP) over the manifold and the associated differential processes. Predictive inference on these rates is devised conditioned on the realized process over the manifold. Manifolds arise as polyhedral meshes in practice. The success of our simulation experiments for assessing derivatives for processes observed over such meshes validate our theoretical findings. By enhancing our understanding of GPs on manifolds, this manuscript unlocks a variety of potential applications in machine learning and statistics where GPs have seen wide usage. We propose a fully model-based approach to inference on the differential processes arising from a spatial process from partially observed or realized data across scattered location on a manifold.
item.dc:creator: Didong Li, Aritra Halder, Sudipto Banerjee

item.title: Conditional Independence under Infinite Measures and Poisson Point Processes
item.description: arXiv:2604.01399v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study conditional independence under infinite measures on punctured product spaces, a notion recently introduced for graphical modeling in multivariate extremes and L\'evy processes. In contrast to classical probabilistic conditional independence, this concept is formulated through normalized restrictions of an infinite measure, a formulation that reflects the non-product structure of the punctured space. We show that this non-standard notion admits a natural probabilistic characterization: it is equivalent to classical conditional independence between coordinate projections of a Poisson point process defined on the punctured space with the given infinite measure as its mean measure. In addition, we provide a functional characterization of the conditional independence concept at the level of the enumerated points of the Poisson point process. We further extend the characterization to punctured products of Borel spaces with distinguished points and a product localization.
item.dc:creator: Shuyang Bai, Vishal Routh

item.title: Principal Manifold Estimation with Riemannian Templates
item.description: arXiv:2604.04272v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Principal manifold estimation (PME) has been successfully applied to robotics and neuroimaging. However, the existing PME framework does not directly accommodate manifolds with non-Euclidean topology, and its theoretical foundations remain incomplete. In this article, we develop a complete theoretical framework for PME that summarizes high-dimensional point clouds using low-dimensional manifolds with general, potentially non-Euclidean topology. The choice of topology can be informed by topological data analysis. Drawing on the theory of Sobolev spaces on Riemannian manifolds, we establish that the proposed principal manifolds are well-defined, prove convergence of the iterative algorithm used to compute them, and establish the consistency of the finite-sample estimator. We further provide a Bayesian interpretation of PME that connects the framework to recent developments in Gaussian processes on Riemannian manifolds. Examples illustrate how the proposed PME framework can be applied to existing statistical methods, including manifold-valued regression. Numerical experiments illustrate the proposed methodology, its computational implementation, and its theoretical properties.
item.dc:creator: Kun Meng, Christopher Perez

item.title: Self-organized regime switching in null-recurrent dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2604.25368v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Based on discrete observations $X_0,X_{\Delta},\dots, X_{n\Delta}$ for $\Delta=n^{-\gamma}$ with $\gamma\in [0,1)$ of the null-recurrent dynamic $dX_t = \sigma(X_t)dW_t$ with a Brownian motion $W$ and $\sigma(x)=\alpha\mathbb{1}\{x<\rho\} + \beta\mathbb{1}\{x\geq \rho\}$, we derive rate of convergence and limiting distribution of the profile MLE for $\rho$. This includes low-frequency asymptotics ($\gamma=0$) for which the observations form a null-recurrent Markov chain. The derived non-standard limit is the argsup over a doubly stochastic drifted Poisson process explicitly involving the local time of oscillating Brownian motion. Its dependence on $\rho$ as well as the unknown volatility levels $\alpha$ and $\beta$ is shown to be continuous w.r.t. the topology of weak convergence, enabling statistical inference. Whereas this limit is independent of the sampling frequency, the profile MLE's rate of convergence equals $n^{-(1+\gamma)/2}$ and is proven to be minimax optimal. The surprising idea of the proof of the limit theorem is to relate the long-term behavior of the null-recurrent Markov chain to the infill asymptotics on a fixed time interval. Indeed, in the very special case that $(X_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is started in the true parameter $X_0=\rho_0$, the process $(X_t-\rho_0)_{t\geq 0}$ is shown to possess a desirable distributional self-similarity. On basis of the strong Markov property, the artificial constellation of starting in $\rho_0$ is finally overcome by a coupling argument.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Brutsche, Sebastian Hahn, Angelika Rohde

item.title: Extended Wasserstein-GAN Approach to Causal Distribution Learning: Density-Free Estimation and Minimax Optimality
item.description: arXiv:2605.10206v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Distributional causal inference requires estimating not only average treatment effects but also interventional outcome distributions, including quantiles, tail risks, and policy-dependent uncertainty. As a method for distributional causal inference, generative adversarial network (GAN)-based counterfactual methods are flexible tools for this task. However, these methods have several limitations. First, the objectives of certain techniques do not coincide with the statistical risk of the identifiable causal target, and therefore provide limited theoretical guarantees regarding estimable counterfactual distributions or optimality. Second, implementing target-design risks under observational sampling can require density-ratio estimation. In this paper, we propose GANICE (GAN for Interventional Conditional Estimation) with several advantages: it (i) specifies the conditional interventional distribution for each treatment--covariate state as the causal estimation target; (ii) estimates the conditional distribution such that its averaged Wasserstein risk is minimized; (iii) attains minimax optimality. GANICE achieves these advantages through the extended Wasserstein distance and cell-normalized estimation, with minimax bounds based on Wasserstein GAN oracle inequalities and an anisotropic Assouad construction; Besov theory characterizes the cellwise critics. Our experiments show that GANICE outperforms existing methods on most benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Shu Tamano, Masaaki Imaizumi

item.title: Measuring multivariate maximal tail dependence
item.description: arXiv:2605.25766v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The classical tail dependence coefficient (TDC) may fail to capture non-exchangeable features of bivariate tail dependence since it evaluates the underlying copula only along the diagonal. To address this limitation, several measures of strongest manifestation of tail dependence have been proposed in the bivariate case, including a measure based on the tail copula of the underlying bivariate copula. This paper introduces and investigates the multivariate maximal tail concordance measure (MTCM), which extends the bivariate measure to the multivariate case. The MTCM quantifies the largest tail mass over lower hyperrectangles of common unit volume, while the associated maximizer identifies the direction of maximal tail probability. We establish fundamental properties of the MTCM in the multivariate case, including existence of an optimal direction. We also derive analytical representations for several important model classes. Closed-form expressions are further obtained for survival Marshall-Olkin copulas, Archimax and nested Archimedean copulas with regularly varying Archimedean generators. An application to trivariate annual sea-level maxima in England reveals off-diagonal stress directions and differences in extremal dependence that are not summarized by likelihood values or the TDC alone. A basis-risk analysis of a parametric insurance further shows that the fitted model with relatively low values of TDC and MTCM can nevertheless yield the most conservative risk assessment due to its non-exchangeability in the tail.
item.dc:creator: Takaaki Koike, Marius Hofert, Haruki Tsunekawa

item.title: Sequential testing of conditionally constrained hypotheses
item.description: arXiv:2606.06769v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterise e-processes for testing non-parametric hypotheses that require the conditional mean of a finite-dimensional statistic to lie in a prescribed convex set. Our main result is a complete-class theorem: every such e-process is pointwise dominated by a predictable product of affine one-step e-variables. Consequently, restricting to test supermartingales entails no loss: at any rejection threshold, the dominating process rejects no later on any observation path. We further show that a minimal complete class exists and consists of predictable products of maximal affine one-step e-variables. These results extend previous complete-class results from single-step constrained testing and bounded one-dimensional conditional mean testing to a broader conditional sequential setting.
item.dc:creator: Eugenio Clerico

item.title: Order restricted estimation of the parameter functions in an additive hazard model
item.description: arXiv:2606.23882v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we propose estimators of the parameter functions in an Aalen additive hasard regression model. The estimators are the individual and component wise $l^2$ projections of the naive estimators resulting from the ordinary least squares estimator in the Aalen additive hazard model on the space of monotone functions. The explicit restrictions imposed on the parameter function by our method have a clear clinical interpretation as they can be used to model early onset or late onset covariate effects on complex diseases. We provide point wise limit distribution results for the resulting estimators, that exhibit $n^{1/3}$ rate of convergence and the Chernoff distribution as the limit distribution. We also provide an asymptotic minimax lower bound showing that our suggested estimators are rate optimal, as well as provide an asymptotic minimax lower bound for the more general problem of estimating a monotone hasard function.
item.dc:creator: Dragi Anevski, ElBatoul Manel Merai

item.title: Toward a Unified Statistical Theory of Multi-View Pretraining for Neural Knowledge Graph Learning
item.description: arXiv:2607.26346v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Knowledge graph learning offers a powerful framework for representing and inferring structured knowledge, with broad practical applications. Two obstacles limit current methods: labeled triples are scarce for each entity and relation, which makes expressive models hard to train, and scoring functions are designed ad hoc, which limits their generalizability and leaves them without theoretical grounding. We address both obstacles with a theoretically grounded framework, with end-to-end guarantees, that extends and subsumes existing methods. The framework proceeds in two stages: multi-view unsupervised pretraining that integrates heterogeneous sources of entity side information into a shared representation, followed by supervised learning across multiple relation types. We establish a unified nonasymptotic risk bound that combines the subspace recovery error of pretraining and the sample complexity of the labeled data in a single guarantee, quantifying formally how large-scale unlabeled data from multiple views benefits downstream knowledge prediction. Synthetic experiments validate each component of the theory, and experiments on large-scale real-world knowledge graph benchmarks confirm the effectiveness of our approach.
item.dc:creator: Jifan Zhang, Miklos Racz, Suqi Liu

item.title: Adaptive Inference for Functionals of M-Estimands
item.description: arXiv:2609.39274v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reinforcement learning and contextual bandit algorithms have become increasingly common in sequential decision-making applications. When these methods are deployed in high-stakes domains, there is growing interest not only in learning effective policies, but also in conducting statistical inference for quantities learned under adaptive data collection. However, classical procedures applied naively in these settings can fail: even when estimators are unbiased, their variance becomes path-dependent and as a result may not be asymptotically normal. A growing literature has emerged to ameliorate this problem, but solutions tend to be problem specific and often rely on correct specification of a working model. In this work, we develop a unified framework for constructing asymptotically valid confidence intervals to cover smooth functionals of nonparametric M-estimands under adaptive sampling. Under Neyman orthogonality, we provide two novel methods for performing inference: (1) a self-normalized statistic based on the realized quadratic variation of the influence function and (2) a statistic using a plug-in estimate of the conditional variance based on reweighted influence function increments. Our results allow for flexible nonparametric estimation of nuisance parameters and remain valid under model misspecification. Our theory is supported by a simulation study for a dynamic pricing application which demonstrates that this method can produce asymptotically valid confidence intervals where standard methods fail.
item.dc:creator: James Leiner, Aur\'elien Bibaut, Nathan Kallus, Aaditya Ramdas, Koulik Khamaru

item.title: Conventional Inference under Nonstationary Heavy Tailed Fractional Processes & Arrays
item.description: arXiv:2610.25237v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing regression inference methods for nonstationary heavy tailed data are largely limited to unit roots tests. Functional central limit theorems (FCLTs), which are commonly used for the asymptotic analysis of nonstationary models, are inapplicable to nonstationary data characterized by a memory parameter $d<1$ and a stability parameter $\alpha<2$. Furthermore, it is well known that inference under nonstationarity is often non-conventional, and this issue is exacerbated in the presence of heavy-tailed data. The interaction of long memory and heavy tails significantly enlarges the nonstationary region---i.e., the covariate model space---where conventional inference methods typically fail. To address these challenges, we propose a new limit theory and methods that facilitate both workable asymptotics and conventional inference in parametric regressions involving stationary and nonstationary heavy-tailed covariate processes. Specifically, our approach develops a limit theory for three classes of heavy-tailed weakly nonstationary processes (hereafter, HT-WNPs), which lie on the threshold of nonstationarity (cf. Duffy and Kasparis, 2021, Annals of Statistics). We also develop limit theory for functionals of strongly nonstationary heavy-tailed fractional processes. We demonstrate that the proposed methods, particularly a weighted extension of IVX, facilitate conventional inference for a broad class of stationary and nonstationary heavy-tailed covariates. This class includes mildly and nearly integrated arrays, as well as nonstationary fractional processes with memory parameter $1-1/\alpha<d<2-1/\alpha$, where $\alpha\in(1,2]$. A related weighted instrumental-variable estimator is also considered, primarily for estimation purposes.
item.dc:creator: Ioannis Kasparis (University of Cyprus)

item.title: A Note on the Finite-Exceedance Dependence Principle for Sum--Maximum Asymptotic Independence
item.description: arXiv:2611.03351v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Asymptotic independence between sum-type and maximum-type statistics arises repeatedly across many areas of probability and statistics, particularly in high-dimensional testing and random matrix theory. Motivated by the shared structure underlying existing proofs, which is obscured by their model-specific formulations, this note isolates a common intermediate principle. We introduce a finite-exceedance dependence principle: if the finite-exceedance dependence error vanishes at every fixed order and high-order exceedances are mildly controlled, then a finite-order Bonferroni argument yields asymptotic independence between the sum and the maximum. We further give an independent-proxy criterion for verifying this: for each finite set of exceedances, it suffices to construct an exactly independent proxy for the sum-type statistic whose approximation error is negligible in aggregate. Local deletion under dependency graphs and Gaussian regression and residualization are two examples. The framework gives modular derivations of existing sum--max independence results.
item.dc:creator: Hongjian Shi

item.title: High-Dimensional Markov-Switching Ordinary Differential Processes
item.description: arXiv:2501.00087v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Complex systems often evolve in continuous time but are observed only at discrete time points with measurement noise. When the interactions can change across unobserved states, recovering both the state transitions and the differential equations is important for mechanistic insight and for identifying time-varying directed graphs. However, this recovery is challenging in high dimensions. In this paper, we study estimation and graph recovery for high-dimensional Markov-switching ordinary differential equation models from noisy discrete observations. We model the switching between states by a latent continuous-time Markov chain, and within each state the drift is a sparse additive function with unknown nonlinear components. We approximate each component by a finite basis expansion and estimate the parameters under group sparsity. Our procedure estimates the latent trajectories by wavelet smoothing and then runs a penalized surrogate expectation-maximization algorithm. Under stationarity and geometric $\beta$-mixing, given a sufficiently accurate estimated trajectory and other local regularity conditions, we show that the algorithm converges geometrically to a neighborhood of the true parameters. Finally, in an application to resting-state fMRI data, the procedure identifies multiple connectivity states, whose occupation times we compare descriptively between the children with combined-type ADHD and the typically developing children used in the fit.
item.dc:creator: Katherine Tsai, Mladen Kolar, Sanmi Koyejo

item.title: Guaranteed Noisy CP Tensor Recovery via Riemannian Optimization on the Segre Manifold
item.description: arXiv:2510.00569v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recovering a low-CP-rank tensor from noisy linear measurements is a central challenge in high-dimensional data analysis, with applications spanning tensor PCA, scalar-on-tensor regression, tensor-on-tensor regression, and beyond. We exploit the intrinsic geometry of rank-one tensors by casting the recovery task as an optimization problem over the Segre manifold, the smooth Riemannian manifold of rank-one tensors. This geometric viewpoint yields two powerful algorithms: Riemannian Gradient Descent (RGD) and Riemannian Gauss-Newton (RGN), each of which preserves feasibility at every iteration. Under mild noise assumptions, we prove that RGD converges at a local linear rate, while RGN exhibits an initial local quadratic phase followed by linear refinement to the statistical error. Extensive synthetic experiments validate these convergence guarantees and demonstrate the practical effectiveness of our methods.
item.dc:creator: Ke Xu, Yuefeng Han

item.title: Debiased Kernel Estimation of Spot Volatility in the Presence of Infinite Variation Jumps
item.description: arXiv:2510.14285v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Volatility estimation is a central problem in financial econometrics, but becomes particularly challenging when jump activity is high, a phenomenon observed empirically in highly traded financial securities. In this paper, we revisit the problem of spot volatility estimation for an It\^o semimartingale with jumps of unbounded variation. We construct truncated kernel-based estimators and debiased variants that extend rate-optimal spot volatility estimation to a wider range of jump activity indices, from the previously available bound $Y<4/3$ to $Y<20/11$. Rate-suboptimal CLTs are also established for $Y>20/11$. Compared with earlier work, our approach achieves smaller asymptotic variances through the use of more general kernels and an optimal choice for the bandwidth convergence rate, and also has broader applicability under more flexible model assumptions. A comprehensive simulation study confirms that our procedures outperform competing methods in finite samples.
item.dc:creator: B. Cooper Boniece, Jos\'e E. Figueroa-L\'opez, Tianwei Zhou

item.title: Structure-Adaptive Estimation of Heterogeneous Treatment Effects with Kernel Methods
item.description: arXiv:2602.18958v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study conditional average treatment effect (CATE) estimation from observational data in regimes with potentially weak overlap, when the nuisance response functions lie in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), but the contrast function is structurally simpler. We consider three forms of such simplicity: (i) membership in a lower-complexity RKHS with faster eigenvalue decay, (ii) a source condition relative to the nuisance kernel, or (iii) dependence on a known low-dimensional covariate representation. We develop a unified two-stage kernel ridge regression procedure that remains valid under weak overlap and attains minimax rates determined by the complexity of the contrast function. The procedure avoids propensity-score estimation and separate nuisance convergence-rate assumptions. We also show that a simple model-selection step over candidate contrast spaces and regularization levels satisfies an oracle inequality, enabling adaptation to unknown CATE regularity.
item.dc:creator: Seok-Jin Kim

item.title: Maximin Robust Bayesian Experimental Design
item.description: arXiv:2603.14094v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We address the brittleness of Bayesian experimental design under model misspecification by formulating the problem as a max--min game between the experimenter and an adversarial nature subject to information-theoretic constraints. We demonstrate that this approach yields a robust objective governed by Sibson's $\alpha$-mutual information~(MI), which identifies the $\alpha$-tilted posterior as the robust belief update and establishes the R\'enyi divergence as the appropriate measure of conditional information gain. To mitigate the bias and variance of nested Monte Carlo estimators needed to estimate Sibson's $\alpha$-MI, we adopt a PAC-Bayes framework to search over stochastic design policies, yielding rigorous high-probability lower bounds on the robust expected information gain that explicitly control finite-sample error.
item.dc:creator: Hany Abdulsamad, Sahel Iqbal, Christian A. Naesseth, Takuo Matsubara, Adrien Corenflos

item.title: Fast Rates for Offline Contextual Bandits with Forward-KL Regularization under Single-Policy Concentrability
item.description: arXiv:2605.09214v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: \emph{Kullback-Leibler} (KL) regularization is ubiquitous in reinforcement learning algorithms in the form of \emph{reverse} or \emph{forward} KL. Recent studies have demonstrated $\epsilon^{-1}$-type fast rates for decision making under reverse KL regularization, in contrast to the standard $\epsilon^{-2}$-type sample complexity. However, for forward-KL-regularized objectives, existing statistical analyses are either not applicable or result in $\tilde{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ slow rates. We take the first step towards addressing this problem via a streamlined analysis of forward-KL-regularized offline CBs. We give the first $\tilde{O}(\epsilon^{-1})$ upper bounds in tabular and general function approximation settings, both under notions of \emph{single-policy concentrability}. In particular, our convex-analytical pipeline unifies these settings by exploiting the pessimism principle in a novel way and completely bypasses the proof routines in previous works based on the mean value theorem, which might be of independent interest. Moreover, we provide rate-optimal lower bounds, manifesting the tightness of our upper bounds in terms of statistical rates. Our lower bounds also demonstrate that the forward-KL-regularized sample complexity recovers the unregularized slow rate in the low-regularization regime, similarly to the reverse-KL regularization.
item.dc:creator: Qingyue Zhao, Kaixuan Ji, Heyang Zhao, Quanquan Gu

item.title: Nearest-Neighbor Radii under Dependent Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2605.14343v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Nearest-neighbor methods are fundamental to classical and modern machine learning, yet their geometric properties are typically analyzed under independent sampling. In this paper, we study the nearest-neighbor radii under dependent sampling. We consider strong mixing dependent observations and ask whether dependence changes the scale of nearest-neighbor neighborhoods. We establish distribution-free almost sure convergence under polynomial mixing and sharp non-asymptotic moment bounds under geometric mixing. The moment bounds depend on the local intrinsic dimension rather than the ambient dimension, making the results applicable to high-dimensional data supported on lower-dimensional manifolds. Synthetic experiments and real-world time-series benchmarks illustrate the theory, showing that nearest-neighbor geometry remains informative under dependent sampling.
item.dc:creator: Yuanyuan Gao, Yilong Hou, Zhexiao Lin

item.title: An Exact Marginal Likelihood for Inference under Careless Responding
item.description: arXiv:2605.26723v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Careless or insufficient-effort responding threatens the validity of self-report measurement. Mixture models for careless responding specify its form, and screening rules and robust methods depend on a threshold or tuning constant with no direct meaning in terms of careless responses. We propose ExHuber, a Bayesian method for inference on the engaged population under Huber's contamination model, in which an unknown proportion of responses comes from a contaminating distribution of unspecified form instead of the structural model. With a finite support of responses, such as the values of a scale score, a Dirichlet prior and a Beta prior on the contaminating distribution and its proportion yield a closed-form exact marginal likelihood of the structural parameters. Under a prior favoring a contaminating distribution on a few values, we show that the posterior of the structural parameters is consistent when careless responses occupy few values of the support, without knowing which values. Dynamic programming evaluates the marginal likelihood and its gradient at a cost quadratic in the sample size, which enables gradient-based sampling. Simulations from graded response models show accurate inference under straightlining and repeated response patterns, and an application to Big Five scales estimates the engaged mean of each scale.
item.dc:creator: Jaehoan Kim

item.title: Weighted Conformal Clustering
item.description: arXiv:2606.00436v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Clustering is a central tool for discovering latent structure in unlabeled data; yet modern clustering pipelines often end with a hard assignment of each observation to a cluster without rigorous measures of assignment uncertainty. We propose a novel weighted conformal approach for constructing valid confidence sets for cluster labels. The key difficulty is that the labels available for calibration are not observed ground-truth labels, but synthetic labels produced by a data-dependent clustering algorithm. Our method develops a conformal inference algorithm that corrects the resulting mismatch with the latent target labels through weights by formulating conformal clustering as a conditional label-distribution shift problem. We first derive an oracle procedure that attains finite-sample marginal coverage and then develop a computationally tractable and implementable version using estimated conditional label probabilities and novel augmented calibration. We show that the coverage of the estimated-weight procedure depends on the estimator, giving an explicit bound on the loss relative to the nominal level. Empirical studies demonstrate that the proposed weighted approach offers improvements over the recently proposed split conformal clustering procedure in terms of informative confidence set size, especially in nonlinear and high-dimensional clustering applications.
item.dc:creator: Anirban Nath, YoonHaeng Hur, Genevera I. Allen

item.title: Express Language Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2606.10944v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a new tool, Express, for converting a non-causal attention approximation into a causal approximation with matching approximation guarantees. When combined with the state-of-the-art Thinformer approximation, Express improves upon the best known causal attention guarantees, delivering $\log^{3/2}(n)/s$ approximation error with only $O(s)$ memory and $O(s^2 \log^2(n))$ compression overhead for a sequence of length $n$. We pair these developments with an efficient I/O-aware Triton implementation, demonstrate substantial speedups over FlashAttention 2, and use Express to overcome four resource bottlenecks in the language modeling pipeline: long-context prefill, KV cache compression, long-form memory-constrained decoding, and long-form compute-constrained decoding.
item.dc:creator: Albert Gong, Annabelle Michael Carrell, Raaz Dwivedi, Lester Mackey

item.title: Causal Inference for All: Marginal Estimands for Outcomes Truncated by Death
item.description: arXiv:2607.00222v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In longitudinal studies, outcomes of interest are often truncated by death, meaning that they are only observed or well-defined conditional on intercurrent events such as survival.
